text:
Asha: Heads-up — we've got a ~3x spike in tool-call schema errors from a single customer slice since 03:00 UTC. Most are 'missing_field: result' but the payload has 'status' + 'payload' instead.
Ben: Hmm, is that a model variant returning a different envelope or failing our validator?
Asha: Validator marks these as HARD rejects currently, so requests are routed to fallback model which costs about 2x and raises latency.
Evelyn: Can you paste an example output?
Asha: Sure:
```
{"status": "ok", "payload": {"text": "..."}, "meta": {"len": 120}}
```
Ben: So the model is returning a different contract. Previously we expected {"result": {...}}.
Cara: Product question — What's the user-visible behavior? Do they get an error or degraded output?
Asha: End users get the fallback model output, which is fine for now but cost + latency are increasing. Some callers rely on the 'result' key and crash downstream (small but real).
Dan: From telemetry side we currently emit validator.failures.total and tool.invoke.fallback.count separately. There's no canonical tag for 'soft_reject' vs 'hard_reject'. We treat all validation failures as fatal.
Ben: We should add a "validation.outcome" tag: values = ["pass","soft_reject","hard_reject"]. Soft_reject would mean we accept the response but mark it and optionally route to fallback.
Evelyn: Agree. For ML teams we sometimes want to tolerate minor envelope drift (extra keys, renamed wrapper) but still flag for retraining.
Cara: UX: Console should show these as "recoverable tool mismatch" with ability to toggle 'treat as fatal' per route. Also need counts by customer, model, and rollout slice.
Asha: Proposed immediate changes: 1) validator returns a classification string (pass/soft/hard) 2) routing policy uses that classification + route config to decide fallback vs accept 3) telemetry emits validation.outcome and validation.reason for sampling.
Ben: Implementation note: validator currently runs in runtime before we decide routing. We'll return a small enum in the invoke response: `validate_result: "soft_reject"` and `validation_reason: "missing_result_key"`.
Dan: I'll add metrics: `toolcall.validation_outcome{outcome=...}` and a histogram `toolcall.latency_by_validation_outcome`. Also want traces sampled when outcome != pass: `trace.sample_rate = 1.0` for hard_reject, 0.05 for soft_reject.
Cara: Console wire: add a per-route toggle: `treat_schema_mismatch_as_fatal: true|false`. Default to false for canary. Show a small timeline sparkline for soft_reject rate.
Asha: Quota question — do soft_rejects count against customer quota? Right now fallback counts as additional invoke. If we accept soft_reject and avoid fallback, we save quota. But that might mask regressions.
Evelyn: Suggest we do not count soft_rejects as extra quota usage (i.e., do not double-charge) if route config opts-in to 'accept_soft'. But we should emit billing tag `billing.validation_accepted=true|false` so finance can reconcile.
Dan: From billing pipeline perspective we need a stable decision at charge time. If runtime accepts soft_reject and returns single response, charge once. If it triggers fallback, charge fallback too. We'll surface `billing.validation_accepted` in the call record.
Ben: Rollout plan: default validator becomes 'soft by default in canary region' behind feature flag `soft_validate_v1`. Start with 10% of traffic, monitor `toolcall.validation_outcome=soft_reject` and downstream error + crash reports.
Asha: Also adding a console alert when soft_reject rate > 1% and trending up 5% over 1h for any route.
Cara: Product approves the plan. Need docs text: explain tradeoffs and recommended settings for consumer APIs vs internal platform calls. I'll draft.
Evelyn: Can we add an auto-tag to model catalog entries when a model starts returning envelope variants so we can auto-suggest model->adapter mapping?
Ben: Good idea. We can add `model.adaptation_suggested=true` when soft_rejects persist > 100 in 24h for that model-version.
Dan: I'll create the metrics and a dashboard template: per-route validation outcome, cost delta if fallback triggered, and linked traces.
Asha: OK. Who will own runtime change? Ben?
Ben: Yep, I'll do validator enum + routing hook. Planning to land a small API: `invoke(... ) -> { response, validate_result, validation_reason, billing.validation_accepted }`.
Cara: UX owner will be me, Dan will own metrics, Ben runtime, Asha will coordinate rollout + customer comms, Evelyn will monitor model side.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started: soft_validate_v1 -> 10% traffic in us-west-2 :rocket:
Asha: I'll watch slack and datadog for first 30m.
Ben: I'll post a short PR with the API contract and sample log line.
Dan: Dashboard link (wip): https://dash.internal/redwood/toolcall-validation (will add panels shortly)
Asha: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene if any customer impact or unexpected spike. :thumbsup:
